findings.issue: Task 3 and the tech-spec architecture section state the new SecurityConfig should use 'XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler to preserve BREACH mitigation from the current XorServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler'. The actual current SecurityConfig explicitly does NOT use the Xor variant — it uses 'ServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler' and the code comment explicitly documents WHY: 'XorServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler would BREACH-mask only the form-attribute and break the cookie/header round-trip'. So the current code deliberately rejects the Xor handler. If Task 3 implements 'XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler' it will change CSRF validation semantics (from raw-token comparison to XOR-masked comparison), which would break SPA X-XSRF-TOKEN header validation — a security regression, not a preservation.
findings.fix: Task 3 description and implementation hints must specify 'new CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler()' (the servlet equivalent of the current 'ServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler'), NOT 'XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler'. The tech-spec architecture section for SecurityConfig must also be corrected to remove the false claim about 'XorServerCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler' being the current handler. The task should state: preserve the raw-token attribute handler pattern (no BREACH masking) because CookieCsrfTokenRepository writes the raw token to the cookie, and the SPA echoes it back via X-XSRF-TOKEN — XOR masking would break this round-trip.

findings.issue: Task 2 TDD Anchor says 'Tests below already exist as StepVerifier-based versions; rewrite them BEFORE flipping the interfaces (so they fail to compile against the still-Mono<Void> shape)'. But this TDD ordering is incorrect: if tests are rewritten to use 'assertThatCode(() -> service.<method>(...)).doesNotThrowAnyException()' BEFORE the interfaces are flipped, the test code that calls 'service.<method>(...)' on a void-method signature will compile fine against the Mono<Void> interface too — it just discards the return value. Void-returning call sites compile against Mono<Void>-returning methods without error. So the 'tests will fail to compile' red-phase claim is false. The actual TDD anchor only provides behavioral assurance after the flip, not a compile-time red phase.
findings.fix: Remove the false compile-error claim from the TDD Anchor description. Restate: 'Rewrite tests to use assertThatCode() before flipping the interfaces. Tests continue to compile against Mono<Void> shape (discarding the return value is legal), then pass after the flip when return type becomes void.' The behavioral verification step (tests pass on void interface) is still valid.

findings.issue: Task 2 edge cases say 'Mockito stubbing of SubscriberService / FunnelTriggerService in other test files (look for when(subscriberService.upsertFromTelegramUpdate(...)).thenReturn(Mono.empty()) in backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/webhook/)'. However, actual inspection of ProcessTelegramUpdateJobTest.java and TelegramWebhookControllerIT.java shows these tests use '@MockitoSpyBean' on the real NoOp implementations — they do NOT use 'when(...).thenReturn(Mono.empty())'. TelegramWebhookControllerIT line 401 uses 'Mockito.doThrow(...).when(subscriberService).upsertFromTelegramUpdate(...)' — a void-compatible stub pattern that works correctly with both Mono<Void> and void return types. So the Mockito 'MissingMethodInvocationException' risk the task warns about does NOT actually apply here because there are no thenReturn(Mono.empty()) stubs to break. This means the edge case is a false alarm. There is NO extra Mockito stubbing update required in these test files.
findings.fix: Update the edge case note to reflect the actual pattern: tests use @MockitoSpyBean which lets the real NoOp implementation run, plus doThrow() stubs in one test. No thenReturn(Mono.empty()) stubs exist in the webhook test files. The only files that need changes are the 7 listed in the Files section.

findings.issue: Task 3 Details section for GlobalErrorHandler says 'Pull BindingResult via ex.getBindingResult()'. However the actual current GlobalErrorHandler at lines 28-31 calls 'ex.getFieldErrors()' and 'ex.getGlobalErrors()' directly on the exception (NOT via getBindingResult()). While MethodArgumentNotValidException extends BindException which has both patterns, the task description introduces a divergence from the existing code style — the actual code never calls getBindingResult(). The task should say 'call ex.getFieldErrors() and ex.getGlobalErrors() directly on the exception, matching the current WebExchangeBindException call pattern byte-for-byte' to ensure the implementation hint does not accidentally introduce an unnecessary getBindingResult() indirection.
findings.fix: Change the implementation hint from 'Pull BindingResult via ex.getBindingResult() and reuse the same getFieldErrors() + getGlobalErrors() extraction' to 'Call ex.getFieldErrors() and ex.getGlobalErrors() directly on the exception object, identical to the current WebExchangeBindException handler — MethodArgumentNotValidException has both methods directly (it extends BindException)'.
